rounds.response:
Two safe-exit options: covert (recommended if you fear retaliation) — leave when he’s out and go straight to a friend’s house, family or a refuge; announced (only if you truly feel safe) — give a short, non-negotiable notice and leave at the agreed time.  
Before you go, pack essentials (ID, passport, meds, cash, keys, charged phone, spare SIM), copy important documents to cloud/email, save screenshots/call logs to a secure place, tell one trusted person your exact plan and ETA, and arrange transport and somewhere to stay.  
If you do send a final message keep it short and firm (avoid arguing): e.g. “I’ve decided to leave and I won’t be back. Do not contact me; if you come to my address or contact me I will report you to the police.” — but if you fear escalation, do not warn him and leave covertly.  
Contact police for advice (999 if immediate danger; 101 to report/record harassment), get legal advice from Citizens Advice or a solicitor about non-molestation/occupation orders, and call the National Domestic Abuse Helpline on 0808 2000 247 so they can support a safe exit and liaise with MARAC or refuge options.  
Keep everything documented (screenshots, photos, GP notes), tell a trusted friend your safety code word, and if you want I can draft exact short messages or a one-page timed checklist you can save on your phone — call 999 now if you believe he is an immediate danger.
